pluginApiNotes: setBoundVariableForPaint attaches the binding but leaves the paint's raw colour at whatever was passed in; Figma rendered that raw colour, so a paint created as {0,0,0} rendered black despite a correct binding. Fix: write the resolved value into the paint AND bind it. 117 paints were repaired this way.
addComponentProperty with type INSTANCE_SWAP rejects a component publish key and requires the component's node id as defaultValue.
resize() after setting counterAxisSizingMode locks the axis to FIXED — it must be re-set to AUTO afterwards or cloned variants inherit a frozen height.

editComponentProperty cannot change a VARIANT property's defaultValue — the API refuses. The default is fixed by variant ordering at creation time, so order variant values with the code default FIRST when the set is created. Button's Size still defaults to Small because of this.
Instance-swap slots should carry preferredValues so designers get a curated icon list rather than every component in the file.
constraints CANNOT be overridden on an instance ('This property cannot be overridden in an instance'). Set constraints on the icon MASTER; instances inherit. Only fills are overridable per instance.

Set figma.skipInvisibleInstanceChildren = false before any findAll/walk that must reach boolean-hidden nodes. The first unbound-paint audit reported 0 while blind to the hidden checkbox and clear-icon slots; re-running with the flag false was what exposed them.

Setting an INSTANCE_SWAP property to the component that is ALREADY that slot's default resets the layer's overrides: the layer name reverts from 'Start icon' to the master's name ('Icon / PlusOutlined') and the per-variant colour override is dropped, so the icon falls back to the master's own fill. Only set a swap property when the target differs from the slot default. Mitigated by binding every master's fill to a token (below), so the degraded state is a themed colour rather than a raw hex.

REGENERATING THE TOKENS PAGE: clear the page's children, then derive everything from getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync + getLocalVariablesAsync — never from a hardcoded list, or the page drifts from the variables it documents. Group colour variables by name prefix (color/<group>/...), sort members by name, and read each value with valuesByMode[collection.modes[0].modeId]. Bind rather than paint wherever Figma allows: fills via setBoundVariableForPaint, and setBoundVariable on 'width', 'height', 'topLeftRadius'/'topRightRadius'/'bottomLeftRadius'/'bottomRightRadius' and 'strokeWeight' — all of these accept FLOAT variables and succeeded here. Typography specimens are rendered by applying the real text style with setTextStyleIdAsync, then reading style.boundVariables back to label which variables each style consumes. Keep the brand-alias map in the script (sourced from paletteValues.ts comments) since Figma has no field for it.

Absolutely-positioned children that overhang their parent — a floating notch label at y = -8, an outside focus ring — are CLIPPED by every ancestor auto-layout frame, because Figma frames default to clipsContent: true. Compositions that nest such components inside wrapper columns must clear clipsContent on the wrappers, or the overhang silently disappears. Apply effect styles with setEffectStyleIdAsync rather than assigning node.effects, so the shadow stays reviewable in one place.

setBoundVariable works on FLOAT-valued layout fields — 'width', 'height', 'strokeWeight' and the four corner-radius fields — not just padding and itemSpacing. Useful for documentation pages where a bar's size should BE the token rather than merely depict it.

Paint-level `opacity` on a variable-bound paint is DISCARDED by later structural operations — appendChild, resize, and combineAsVariants all re-resolve the paint from its variable. Apply the opacity as the very last step (Object.assign({}, boundPaint, {opacity})) after the node is in its final position, and verify by reading fills[0].opacity back. Setting opacity before binding never survives at all, because setBoundVariableForPaint returns a new paint.

An INSTANCE_SWAP property resolves to its single defaultValue across EVERY variant in the set, discarding whatever instance each variant was authored with. A variant cannot ship a different default control. Either drop the swap property to keep per-variant instances, or keep the swap and document that one variant renders the wrong default until swapped.

Cloning a variant that is ALREADY inside a COMPONENT_SET silently drops all componentPropertyReferences on the clone and every descendant. Nothing throws and setProperties still records values, so overrides just appear to do nothing. Either add properties after all variants exist, or walk source and clone in lockstep and copy references node-for-node. Always verify by counting references per variant, not by eye.

When a component property drives a hugging container's width (a notch gap sizer, a reserved slot), the sizer must mirror EVERY node that can widen the visible element — a label plus its optional asterisk, not just the label. Test the combination where the optional child is on.

Never fake a border interruption with a background-coloured mask — it only holds on the surface colour you assumed. Build a real gap: a horizontal auto-layout of slices using Figma's per-side stroke weights (strokeTopWeight / strokeBottomWeight / strokeLeftWeight / strokeRightWeight) with corner radii on the end slices. A hugging middle slice sized by a transparent text node bound to the label property makes the gap track content automatically.

Set a TEXT node's `name` AFTER assigning `characters`, and never to the literal 'Text'. 'Text' is the default name for a new TEXT node, so assigning it does not clear the autoRename flag and the content overwrites the name. Prefer type-based or index-based lookup over name-based for text inside components you did not just create.

A TEXT node created with empty characters collapses to width 0, and setting layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' afterwards does NOT recover it — the node stays 0 wide and any text later assigned wraps one character per line (a 'Default Value' string produced a 288px-tall input). Fix: set textAutoResize='HEIGHT', resize() to a real width, THEN set FILL. Verify node.width > 0 before trusting the layout.

Every icon master's vector fill is now bound to the token that already matched its literal value (text/primary, primary/main, grey/600, text/secondary, common/white). Appearance is unchanged, but any lost override degrades to a themed colour and the masters pass the unbound-paint audit.

The variables API lives under figma.variables, NOT on the figma global: getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync and getLocalVariablesAsync are figma.variables.* and throw 'no such property' if called directly on figma.

Auto-layout frames accept minWidth / maxWidth / minHeight / maxHeight, which map onto CSS min/max sizing exactly. Tab's minWidth 90, maxWidth 360 and minHeight 48 are expressed with them rather than by faking a fixed size, so a hugging Tab still grows with its label and still bottoms out at 90.

An ELLIPSE's arcData { startingAngle, endingAngle, innerRadius } reproduces an SVG stroke-dasharray ring exactly, and innerRadius is a 0-1 RATIO rather than a dimension — so a ring whose real thickness is fractional (CircularProgress: 3.273px) can be drawn without storing any fractional value on the node. Angle 0 is 3 o'clock going clockwise, which is also where an SVG <circle> path starts, so the two systems line up with no offset.

CSS `transform: translate(50%, -50%)` on an absolutely-positioned child (Badge's anchorOrigin) keeps the child's CENTRE on the anchor point as it grows. Figma has no equivalent, and a plain absolute child grows rightward from its x. Reproduce it with a centring anchor frame: twice the offset wide, auto-layout with primaryAxisAlignItems CENTER, positioned so its own centre is the anchor point. The child then grows symmetrically. The anchor overhangs the parent, so clipsContent must be false on the component AND on every wrapper that nests it.

figma.combineAsVariants leaves the set in whatever layout you give it; for sets whose variants differ a lot in size, setting layoutMode NONE and positioning variants manually in a size-per-row grid produces a far more reviewable variant sheet than layoutWrap WRAP, which packs them raggedly.

A set-level TEXT component property forces ONE default across every variant, exactly like INSTANCE_SWAP. Adding Title/Body properties to a set whose variants carry different copy silently overwrites all of it with the property default — the variant heights collapse and the axis stops meaning anything. Caught only because the post-combine heights differed from the pre-combine ones. If variants differ by their text, do not expose that text as a property; instance text stays editable without one.
figma.createNodeFromSvg gives its wrapper frame an opaque white fill that the source SVG does not declare. Walking frame.children misses it — walk the frame itself, or clear it explicitly.

createNodeFromSvg DOES accept an embedded base64 data-URI <image>, producing a RECTANGLE with an IMAGE fill, even though createImageAsync is unavailable. Probe with a 1x1 PNG before assuming an illustration must be stripped.

Figma imports an SVG <clipPath> as a mask group and discards the clip shape fill, defaulting it to black. The shape still renders nothing (masks use alpha), but it reads as an unbound black paint in an audit. Bind it to whatever the source declares.

GROUP and BOOLEAN_OPERATION bounds are derived from their contents, so they are fractional whenever the contained geometry is. They cannot be authored to integers and must be excluded from an all-dimensions-integer check, exactly as VECTOR already is.

Set textAutoResize AFTER characters, not before: on a node whose characters are set later, an earlier textAutoResize=HEIGHT does not survive, and the block renders as one unwrapped line. Order is fontName -> characters -> setTextStyleIdAsync -> textAutoResize -> resize.
setTextStyleIdAsync resets textDecoration. Apply UNDERLINE after the text style, and re-apply it after any later characters assignment.

A COMPONENT_SET's default variant is resolved by CANVAS POSITION — the top-left-most variant wins — NOT by child array order. Reordering in the layers panel changes children[] and leaves x/y alone, so the default does not move and the canvas looks unchanged; the set will still report the old defaultValue and instances will still resolve to it. To change a variant default you must move the target variant so it is the top-left node. Confirmed 2026-08-03 on Button, where a layers-panel reorder had put Size=Medium at children[0] while Size=Small stayed at (32,32) and every new instance still came out Small. editComponentProperty cannot change a VARIANT default either — position is the only lever.

resize() on a TEXT node silently resets textAutoResize to 'NONE'. Set the mode AFTER the resize, not before, or the node stops growing with its content — and because it stops growing rather than erroring, the overflow is invisible until an ancestor with clipsContent cuts it off. Cost a clipped REFERENCE note on 2026-08-03; the same shape as the resize()-locks-the-sizing-axis trap already recorded for auto-layout frames.

iconRecipe._why: Took three rounds to converge. Regressing any step visibly breaks icons. Apply to every new icon master and every icon slot.
iconRecipe.1_viewBoxPosition: Vectors must keep their imported viewBox position inside the 24x24 frame — do NOT reset x/y to 0. createNodeFromSvg already positions them correctly; just move them into the component. Verified positions: DownCaret (2, 6.49), Cancel (2, 2), Close-MUI (5, 5), TrashOutlined (2.52, 2), Checkbox (3, 3).
iconRecipe.2_scaleConstraints: Every vector gets constraints {horizontal:'SCALE', vertical:'SCALE'} so the glyph scales like an SVG viewBox. CENTER centres but does not scale, which renders oversized when the frame is set to 16px. Must be set on the master — see pluginApiNotes.
iconRecipe.3_colorInheritance: Figma has no currentColor. Clone the source text paint onto every icon vector per variant, carrying BOTH the resolved colour and the boundVariables together (cloning only the binding reproduces the black-paint gotcha). White knockout shapes inside a glyph must be skipped so they stay white.
iconRecipe.layerNaming: Vector layers must be named 'Vector' — instance-swap overrides only survive across components with matching layer names.

chipCommonConfigurations._whatItIs: A strip of INSTANCES, not masters, showing the three configurations designers reach for. Labelled as instances so nobody mistakes them for additional components or tries to publish them.

configurations.label: Deletable
configurations.props: Size=Medium, Variant=Filled, Color=Default, State=Default, Delete icon = true

configurations.label: Clickable
configurations.props: Size=Medium, Variant=Filled, Color=Default, State=Hover — clickable is not a Chip axis; hover IS the clickable affordance, since MUI only applies the hover treatment when onClick is present

configurations.label: Small deletable
configurations.props: Size=Small, Variant=Filled, Color=Default, State=Default, Delete icon = true

chipCommonConfigurations.note: Chip has no Clickable axis in the built set. MUI gates the clickable visual on the presence of onClick, which is a prop not a variant, so the Hover state is the only way the clickable affordance surfaces. Recorded so the strip is not read as a missing axis.

usageAnnotations._method: Balanced-bracket scan of every <Chip> and <Switch> JSX opening tag across 4269 .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx files in C:/Code/web-app-v2 (node_modules, .yarn, dist, build excluded), attributing each prop to its own tag rather than to a context window. Design-system stories counted separately from product sites.
usageAnnotations._rule: ANNOTATE, NEVER DELETE. A variant that code defines but product rarely reaches is still a real API surface; the asymmetry is the deliverable, not a reason to narrow the set.
usageAnnotations._where: Written into the Figma component descriptions on Data display (Chip) and Inputs (Switch), in the form 'code defines X; product usage is Y per <evidence>'.

Switch.codeDefines: Size = medium | small. Switch.stories.tsx:18-23 declares argTypes.size with options ['medium','small']; Switches.args pins size:'medium'. MUI substrate supplies both geometries. SwitchOverrides.ts registers styleOverrides.root only — no size-specific rule, no defaultProps.
Switch.productUsage: MEDIUM ONLY. 13 <Switch> tags across 10 files; every one omits the size prop, so all render at MUI's medium default.
Switch.evidence: rg '<Switch' over web-app-v2 = 13 occurrences in 10 files (VisitReasonsToggle, PatientSurveysReviewsPage, ReserveWithGoogleSection, MessagesPage, AiMessageTagging, GeneralSettings, NewWorklistBody, SettingToggle, ShowHideLabelsList, plus 4 in Switch.stories.tsx). A repo-wide search for a size prop on a Switch tag returns zero. rg 'MuiSwitch' returns only SwitchOverrides.ts, so no theme-level defaultProps sets it either.
Switch.finding: The direction matters: MEDIUM is the size product actually ships and SMALL is the story/argType-only one. Any reading in which Medium is the unused variant is contradicted by source. Reported, not resolved.
Switch.action: Both variants kept. Annotation added to the Switch description.

Chip.codeDefines: Color = default | primary | secondary | error | info | success | warning (seven, from the Chip story's argTypes).
Chip.productUsage: ALL SEVEN are reachable — none is unused — but the distribution is very uneven across 79 product <Chip> tags (85 total, 6 of them in design-system stories).

perColour.primary: 9 literal sites, plus dynamic reaches (SdohPage selected ternary, WebsocketControls, DocumentChip)
perColour.error: 1 authored site — admin-ui/src/components/UserSettings/UserList/UserItem.tsx:127. Every other reach is data-driven: ErxRequestsTab.tsx:20, ErxRequestsDataGrid.tsx:33, OutstandingTasksList.tsx:31, WebsocketControls.tsx:35, CompositionsList/ListItem.tsx:35 statusChipMap, DocumentChip.tsx:69.
perColour.secondary: 2 sites in the entire monorepo — documents-ui/src/components/MergeIssuesTabLabel.tsx:13 (literal) and messages-ui/src/components/SideMenu/NavItem/SideMenuNavItem.tsx:65 (via badgeColor, whose other branch is 'default'). Rarest by an order of magnitude.
perColour.default: Never written literally on a Chip tag. It is what 19 product tags get by omitting color entirely, plus the ?? 'default' fallbacks in ClinicalBlockNodeView.tsx:36 and SdohPage.tsx:175.

Chip.sizeUsage: 39 product tags set size='small'; 38 omit size and render Medium. Both real.
Chip.variantUsage: 14 literal outlined, 1 literal filled, 56 omit variant and render filled. Both real.
Chip.finding: 'Unused chip colours' does not hold as stated — every one of the seven is reachable in shipped product. The defensible version of the observation is narrower: secondary is rare (2 sites) and error is almost entirely data-driven rather than authored.
Chip.action: Nothing deleted. All 84 variants kept. Annotation added to the Chip description.
